requirements.evidence: Only skeletons exist: Entity/EntityMembership models (app/Models/Entity.php:1-37), enum, factories and two migrations; several fatal errors and missing pieces make the feature unusable: wrong base class app/Http/Controllers/EntityController.php:11, wrong HasFactory import app/Models/Entity.php:5, invalid generated-column SQL database/migrations/20231029000001_create_entity_memberships_table.php:30, enum/string policy comparisons app/Policies/EntityPolicy.php:38 and app/Policies/EntityMembershipPolicy.php:23, missing route names routes/web.php:54-56, no lang keys, no docs update.

conventions.evidence: No tests in the diff (conventions.md:12-21); inline `$this->validate([...])` instead of `#[Validate]` (app/Livewire/Entity/Members.php:26, app/Livewire/Entity/Settings.php:30); no `#[Locked]` on server-context properties (app/Livewire/Entity/Settings.php:15); domain writes inline instead of app/Actions (app/Livewire/Entity/Settings.php:42-70); docs/database-schema.md and CHANGELOG.md untouched (conventions.md:92-103).

security.evidence: `addMember()` never authorizes (app/Livewire/Entity/Members.php:24-39); `save()`, `delete()` and `transfer()` only rely on mount and the `Entity $entity` public property is not `#[Locked]`, so the client can swap entities (app/Livewire/Entity/Settings.php:15,28-70); owner protection checks compare an enum cast to `->value` strings and are always false (app/Policies/EntityMembershipPolicy.php:23,31,35), letting the owner be demoted or self-deleted; no action re-authorizes after mount.

tests.evidence: change.diff contains no files under tests/ (768-line diff ends at routes/web.php:56); no happy-path, validation, unauthorized-call or tamper test for any model, policy, migration, EntityController::pick or Livewire action.

simplicity.evidence: Components are short, but the change duplicates membership lookups, adds a redundant custom `Route::bind('entity')` next to `{entity:slug}` (routes/web.php:45-47), carries unused imports (app/Livewire/Entity/Members.php:10-11, app/Http/Controllers/EntityController.php:6) and hand-rolls dialect-specific SQL instead of a supported schema/DB feature (database/migrations/20231029000001_create_entity_memberships_table.php:29-34).

readability.evidence: Methods are short and names are clear, but there are dead imports, stale planning comments (database/migrations/20231029000001_create_entity_memberships_table.php:22-28), misleading enum/string comparisons (app/Policies/EntityMembershipPolicy.php:22-23) and hard-coded UI strings (resources/views/livewire/entity/settings.blade.php:5,9,11).

scope.evidence: All new application files serve the entities task, but routes/web.php also contains unrelated churn: import reshuffle (:3-8), a `// Default routes` comment (:10), the logout route rewritten to FQCN (:24) and reflowed e-mail verification routes (:40-42).

issues.explanation: It extends `\Illuminate\Foundation\Http\Controller`, which does not exist (the base class is `App\Http\Controllers\Controller`), so the controller cannot be loaded and `entity.pick` fails.

`Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\HasFactory` is not a real class (it lives under `...\Factories\HasFactory`), and the same wrong import is used at app/Models/EntityMembership.php:6, so both models fatal on load.

`Illuminate\Access\HandlesAuthorization` does not exist (correct namespace is `Illuminate\Auth\Access`); the same wrong import is at app/Policies/EntityMembershipPolicy.php:8, so policy instantiation fails.
The `Auth` facade has no `policy()` method (that belongs to `Gate`), so boot() throws a BadMethodCallException and the whole application fails to start.

The generated-column expression `(role = 'owner' ? 1 : NULL)` uses a ternary operator that neither SQLite nor MariaDB supports, and MariaDB cannot index a VIRTUAL generated column, so the required portable owner constraint cannot be created on either target database.

`Entity $entity` is a public, non-`#[Locked]` property and `save()`, `delete()` and `transfer()` never re-authorize, so a client can swap the entity to one they do not own and edit or soft-delete that entity's data; this directly violates the task's 'the bound entity must not be swappable from the client' requirement.
`addMember()` performs no `$this->authorize(...)`, so any member (including an employee) can add users, and the required 403 for employees on add is not enforced.

`$membership->role` and `$current->role` are cast to `UserRole`, but they are compared with `UserRole::...->value` strings, so the owner checks are always false: the owner can be demoted through `assignRole()` or self-deleted through `removeMember()`, leaving an entity with no owner.

The same enum-vs-string comparison makes `update`, `delete` and `manageSettings` always return false, so `Settings::mount()` 403s even for the real owner (app/Livewire/Entity/Settings.php:22) and the settings page is unusable.
`$this->entity->membershipFor($user->id)` calls a method that only exists on `User`, not on `Entity`, so every `addMember()` call throws instead of adding or reporting the duplicate.
`{{ $m->role }}` echoes a `UserRole` enum object, which is not stringable, so Blade's escaping throws and the members page cannot render.

The three Livewire routes are unnamed (`route('entity.dashboard')` etc. are undefined) and have no `auth`/`verified` middleware, so the redirects at app/Http/Controllers/EntityController.php:27 and app/Livewire/Entity/Settings.php:38,69 fail and guests can reach the components.

The dashboard has no welcome text and no owner notice ('Você é o proprietário desta entidade.'), and the settings link's `role === 'owner'` check compares an enum to a string so the link never appears, even for the owner.

No `lang/*/ui.php` changes exist; the required keys (`ui.nav_members`, `ui.nav_settings`, dashboard/transfer texts) and the custom keys (`ui.member_already`, `ui.role_invalid`, `ui.select_owner`, `ui.invalid_target`) are missing, while views hard-code English strings.

`transfer()` returns validation errors instead of 403 for a non-admin/foreign target, and dereferences `$currentOwner` without a null check, so the required 403 when the owner row vanished becomes a 500.
Neither `removeMember()` nor `EntityMembershipPolicy::delete()` implements the 'never removes the last manager -> 403' rule, so the last admin can be removed.
The contract requires `App\Models\UserRole`, but the enum lives in `App\Enums`, and `manageable()` returns string values instead of the required `[Admin, Employee]` cases.
Inside `Database\Factories`, the unqualified `App\Models\Entity::factory()` resolves to a nonexistent namespaced class (no import or leading backslash), so the factory fatals whenever it is used.
No Pest/PHPUnit tests ship with the change at all, despite the test-first convention and the mandatory unauthorized-call and tamper tests for every Livewire action.
The task explicitly requires updating docs/database-schema.md and the conventions require a CHANGELOG entry, but the diff touches neither.

Validation uses inline rule arrays instead of the project's `#[Validate]` + `$this->validate()` pattern, and no server-context property is marked `#[Locked]`, contrary to the Livewire security policy.
Membership IDs are resolved globally with `findOrFail()` and only the policy ties them to an entity, so the component can act on another entity's membership instead of only the mounted entity.
The slug uniqueness rule excludes soft-deleted rows, but the database unique index does not, so saving a slug held by a trashed entity passes validation and then fails at the database.
Entity deletion and ownership transfer are domain writes performed inline in the component instead of in `app/Actions/*` classes that authorize internally, as the conventions require.
The new Blade views use no Bulma classes or reusable components and their inputs/selects have no labels or accessible names, contrary to the Bulma/accessibility conventions.
The route file contains unrelated churn: import reshuffling, a new `// Default routes` comment, the logout route rewritten to a FQCN and reflowed verification routes.
The custom `Route::bind('entity', ...)` duplicates the `{entity:slug}` binding and silently ignores the declared field, adding a second source of truth for entity resolution.
Unused `Auth`/`DB` imports remain in Members and the migration keeps stale planning comments about how the generated column will be added.

review.summary: The change adds the entity data model, enum, factories, policies, one controller, three Livewire components/views and routes, but it is only a rough skeleton: wrong imports and base classes, an unsupported generated-column expression, enum-versus-string policy checks and unnamed/unprotected routes mean much of it cannot run. It also ships no tests, no lang files, no documentation update, and leaves multiple Livewire actions unauthorized and the bound entity client-swappable, so the PR must be rejected.
